transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. I'm Santiago. I'm here because... well, I've been having this issue with eating lately. 

What really worries me is that once I start picking at food late at night, I just can't seem to stop. I'll tell myself, "That's enough, Santiago," but my hand just keeps going back for more. It's almost like I don't get to make the decision anymore.
After one of these late-night eating episodes, do you ever try to 'make up for it'—for example by making yourself vomit, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising intensely?

No, I don't do any of that. I don't make myself throw up or take anything like laxatives. And I definitely don't exercise like crazy or stop eating the next day. I usually just... well, I just feel pretty bad about it the next morning, but I don't try to make up for it like that.
How often would you say these episodes of feeling out of control with eating happen, and how long have you been experiencing this pattern?

Well, for the past several months, I'd say it's been happening most weeks... at least once a week, anyway. It usually happens on a night when there are plenty of leftovers around the kitchen, and everyone else has already gone to bed so I'm just up by myself.
During these late-night eating episodes, would you say you're eating an amount of food that's clearly larger than what most people would eat in that same amount of time?

Yeah, definitely. On some nights after work, I can go through... well, several tamales, a really big bowl of pozole, some tortillas, and just whatever rice or beans are left sitting out. I do all of this just standing there in the kitchen, almost like I'm just... cleaning up the leftovers, you know? But it's a lot of food. It's definitely more than what a normal person would eat in that short amount of time.
Do you find yourself eating alone during these episodes specifically because you feel embarrassed or self-conscious about how much you're eating?

Yeah, that's exactly it. I just... I don't like anyone seeing how much I put away. It's embarrassing. So I wait until my aunt and the rest of the house are asleep, and I just try to keep it quiet in the kitchen so nobody comes out and catches me.
